_note: The room. Read by api/chat.js. The artist's wallets live in data/source/artist.json ... see docs/TAO-CHAT.md.
_min_note: Any TAO at all is a voice. One edition copy held for one day is enough, and that is the point of the threshold being where it is.
_tags_note: How many collectors one message may name. Five is more than a sentence needs and fewer than a shout takes. The tag budget below runs over the same window as the message burst, so ten messages naming five people each runs out of names before it runs out of messages.
_reactions_note: The quick row under a message: cherry, heart, thumb, fire, laugh, star, hundred, red envelope. Eight, and eight is the ceiling ... past that the row is a keyboard rather than a nod. The red envelope is the TAO glyph the Studio header took, so reacting with it is the room saying that is the good stuff in the character it already means it in. The row is no longer the whole vocabulary: the + at its end opens every standard emoji, and anything chosen there attaches exactly like one of these ... one per wallet per message per emoji, the same mono count. Change this list and the row changes with it; marks already left in a mark that has been dropped stay on their messages, because the log is the record.
_image_note: One picture per message. The page resizes to 2000 on the long side and re-encodes through a canvas before sending, which is also what strips the EXIF ... people post from phones and a phone writes where it was standing into the file. The server checks the container rather than taking the page's word for it: what the bytes actually are, and whether any camera data survived. The ceiling here is the resize plus room, not the target.
_reaction_note: Reactions cost a keystroke rather than a sentence, so the fifteen second floor between messages would be absurd here. They get their own budget over the same ten minute window.
_sign_note: Which sentence the wallet is asked to sign. "house" is the one this site wrote: named action, named domain, a date in words. "4361" is the same promise serialized to EIP-4361, because mobile wallets sniff for that shape and hand anything else to a generic signing path ... which is where Rainbow's `an error occurred` lives. The copy survives as the statement and the resources. Both are accepted while a page somebody left open still holds the old one; the page is told which to send, so changing this is a data edit rather than a deploy.
_session_note: One signature opens the room for thirty days. Signing per message is right for a wallet you touch twice a year and wrong for a room ... a hardware wallet tap per sentence is not a conversation. Change this number and nothing else needs changing: the sentence the wallet shows carries the date it works out from here, and never a duration in words.
